grammar[0].fact: *Man* has two forms you need: *einen* and *einem*. *Das macht einen müde.* That makes one tired. *Das sagt einem keiner.* No one tells you that. Germans use them all the time to complain about life in general, and it’s very satisfying.

document.intro: A real notice on a red phone box full of books, in Brühl, near Cologne. There’s no lock and no staff, and the phone is long gone. It’s full of *Sie*, *jemand* and little imperatives.
document.fact: Germany has a great many of these open bookcases, and they really work. People leave crime novels and take crime novels.
reading.intro: Saturday afternoon at a repair café in Kassel. Maya has brought the toaster that always burns one side. At table four sits Herr Rösch, 79, formerly of Siemens. He has already taken it to pieces and is looking at it as a doctor looks at an X-ray.
reading.fact: The first *Repair Café* began in Amsterdam in 2009, and Germany now has very many of them. They are run by volunteers, for free, with a tin for donations. People go for the coffee, for the company, and to be told by an expert that nobody builds them like this any more.
